data.long_meaning: Jaladhi is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'jalada' which means 'carrying water' or 'oceanic'. historical_references.reference: Jaladhi was a prominent Hindu king of the Chalukya dynasty. He ruled from 1132 to 1151 CE. He expanded the Chalukyan empire to its greatest extent by adding the Kalachuri and Yadava territories to his domains.

Jaladhi, also known as Jaladeva, was a Jain Tirthankara, or religious leader, of the 22nd cycle of time in Jain cosmology. He is considered to be the fourth Jina of the present age, and is revered as the embodiment of forgiveness and compassion.
